title: Research Data Series: Index of Common Inflation Expectations

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: The Federal Reserve published a FEDS Note introducing the Index of Common Inflation Expectations (CIE), a dynamic factor model that summarizes comovement across various inflation expectations measures. The data series is updated quarterly and includes estimates through 2020Q4, with planned updates on the third Friday of the first month of each quarter. This is experimental research data with no current market-moving information.
key_points: CIE uses a dynamic factor model to summarize common movements across multiple inflation expectations measures
The index is projected onto Survey of Professional Forecasters (SPF) 10-year PCE inflation and University of Michigan survey 5-10 year expectations
Quarterly updates are posted at noon Eastern Time on the third Friday of January, April, July, and October, unless an FOMC meeting falls on the prior Friday
April 2022 update added NY Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations measures (1-year and 3-year ahead) and Michigan 25th/75th percentiles
Original CIE columns were phased out by October 2022, replaced by updated_CIE_spf and updated_CIE_mich
Series is explicitly labeled as experimental and may be discontinued at any time; for informational purposes only
why_it_matters: This source describes a methodological framework for tracking inflation expectations rather than providing current macro catalysts or market-moving information. The CIE aggregates multiple surveys and market-based measures into a single index, which could be useful for monitoring inflation expectations trends. However, the source itself contains no current data values, only methodology descriptions and historical revision notes.
macro_context: The CIE is designed to capture common movements in inflation expectations, which are a key input for monetary policy assessment. The source describes methodology but contains no current inflation expectations readings.
